original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Record-breaker says London Marathon win was ‘a victory for all of us’ as he is greeted by family and friends in Eldoret

Hugged, cheered and adorned with garlands, the first man to run an official marathon in under two hours has returned as a hero to his home village in Kenya.

Sabastian Sawe, who stunned the world when he clocked 1h 59m 30s in the London Marathon last weekend, flew in a Kenyan military plane normally reserved for special operations on Thursday to his home region of western Kenya.

Waiting on the runway at a small airport perched on top of an escarpment 2,150 metres above sea level, Lydia Sawe was trembling with anxious excitement, hands clasped around a huge bouquet of orange roses, as her husband’s aircraft touched down.

The plane door opened and the 31-year-old runner locked eyes with his wife and, beaming, made a beeline straight for her arms. “Congratulations, darling,” she whispered in his ear, tears streaming down her face.

Sawe, who broke the world record by 65 seconds, signed a visitor book in the little VIP lounge at Eldoret airport and hugged a line of ecstatic friends and locals. He was given a wreath made from the sinendet plant, which symbolises victory within his Kalenjin ethnic group, and fed fermented milk from a gourd by Lydia to celebrate his win.

“The victory that took place last Sunday was not just my victory, it was a victory for all of us’ he said in Kiswahili, addressing the jubilant local community that had gathered to welcome him at the airport entrance. “I’m so happy to be home and … welcomed this much, I’m so grateful,” he told the Guardian.

Famous runners are nothing new to this high-altitude part of Kenya. In the towns and villages around the city of Eldoret, in the Great Rift Valley, life is about farming crops, tending to livestock and nurturing the next generation of world record-breaking distance runners.

Every day, the red dirt roads that weave between modest homesteads and maize fields are pounded by the trainers of thousands of hopeful, driven young runners.

People living in and growing up in Eldoret are often able to become good distance runners as at altitude people produce more red blood cells to deal with the lower-oxygen environment. When competing at lower altitudes, more red blood cells can boost oxygen delivery to muscles, resulting in better endurance and performance.

[Lähde: Yahoo Sports]
Marathon record-breaker Sabastian Sawe has received a hero’s welcome home in Kenya, with fans thronging the airport in Nairobi and the country’s president giving him cash and a car.

Sawe posted the first-ever sub-two-hour marathon time of 1:59:30 when he won the London Marathon on Sunday, shattering one of athletics’ most elusive barriers and improving on the previous world record by more than one minute.

The 31-year-old was the toast of the nation when he arrived home late on Wednesday and was greeted by jubilant fans and family members.

The aircraft carrying Sawe was greeted with a traditional water cannon salute when it landed at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport.

Kenya’s President William Ruto welcomed Sawe at State House and awarded him eight million Kenyan shillings ($62,064) as well as a car.

Chaotic and celebratory scenes awaited Sawe as he gave a short media conference at the airport, according to Al Jazeera’s Catherine Soi.

“People have come to celebrate him, they say that he’s a hero,” Soi reported from the airport, where Sawe’s supporters told Al Jazeera the distance runner had made them proud.

Many fans admitted that they were unaware of Sawe until his feat made the news, and they watched snippets of his race.

“Seeing him in real life was very special, and it was also inspiring for me to know that he’s just an ordinary person like me,” Sawe fan David Gitonga told Al Jazeera.

“If he can achieve such great things, then it means that I also have the potential to do it.”

Others said they were encouraged to push their own limits and “maybe do better” than what Sawe had achieved.

He was welcomed at the airport by his parents and Sports Minister, Salim Mvurya, who hailed the runner’s accomplishment as “a win for Kenya.”

He was adorned with a traditional wreath made from twigs to symbolise victory.

Traditional dancers sang his praises as he then climbed into a luxury government vehicle as part of the “heroic welcome” hailed by the sports minister.

Sawe’s parents said that they knew he was destined for greatness even as a child. His mother recounted how he sprinted during bath time.

payload.title: Sabastian Sawe sai sankarin vastaanoton Keniassa alle kahden tunnin maratonin jälkeen
payload.summary: Sabastian Sawe palasi Keniaan sankarina juostuaan Lontoon maratonin aikaan 1.59.30. Hänet otettiin vastaan perheen ja ystävien ympäröimänä Eldoretissa.
payload.content:
Kenialainen Sabastian Sawe on saanut sankarin vastaanoton kotimaassaan juostuaan Lontoon maratonin aikaan 1.59.30. Aineiston mukaan Sawe on ensimmäinen mies, joka on juossut virallisen maratonin alle kahdessa tunnissa, ja hän palasi saavutuksensa jälkeen kotiseudulleen läntiseen Keniaan.

## Vastaanotto Eldoretissa

Sawea tervehdittiin Eldoretissa perheen ja ystävien ympäröimänä. Vastaanotossa häntä halattiin, kannustettiin ja koristeltiin kukkaseppeleillä. Aineiston mukaan paluu sai sankarillisen sävyn, sillä saavutus oli huomattu laajasti myös Kenian ulkopuolella.

Sawe oli juossut Lontoon maratonin edellisenä viikonloppuna ajassa 1.59.30. Aika kuvataan aineistossa historialliseksi, koska se alitti kahden tunnin rajan virallisessa maratonissa.

Sawe itse kuvasi voittoa yhteiseksi saavutukseksi. Hän sanoi Lontoon maratonin voiton olleen ”voitto meille kaikille”. Kommentti annettiin, kun hänet otettiin vastaan kotiseudullaan.

## Paluu tehtiin sotilaskoneella

Sawe lensi torstaina Kenian armeijan koneella läntisen Kenian kotiseudulleen. Aineiston mukaan kyseessä oli kone, jota käytetään tavallisesti erikoisoperaatioihin.

Lento korostaa sitä, miten poikkeuksellisena saavutusta pidettiin. Aineisto ei kuitenkaan kerro tarkempia tietoja siitä, kuka lennon järjesti, ketkä olivat vastaanottotilaisuudessa mukana tai millaisia virallisia kunnianosoituksia Sawelle mahdollisesti annettiin.

## Saavutus nosti juoksijan kansalliseksi sankariksi

Maratonajan lisäksi uutisen ydin on vastaanotto, jonka Sawe sai palatessaan kotiin. Hänen suorituksensa liitettiin Kenian vahvaan kestävyysjuoksuperinteeseen, mutta aineisto ei sisällä laajempaa taustaa hänen urastaan tai aiemmista saavutuksistaan.

Varmistettu kokonaisuus on, että Sawe juoksi Lontoossa alle kahden tunnin virallisen maratonin, palasi sen jälkeen Keniaan ja sai kotiseudullaan lämpimän vastaanoton perheen, ystävien ja kannattajien keskellä.
summary_bullets: Sabastian Sawe juoksi Lontoon maratonin aikaan 1.59.30.
Hänet otettiin vastaan sankarina kotiseudullaan läntisessä Keniassa.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketin tietoihin Sawen maratonajasta, paluusta Keniaan, vastaanotosta Eldoretissa ja hänen kommentistaan. Tarkempia urataustoja, vastaanoton järjestäjiä tai virallisia kunnianosoituksia ei lisätty, koska niitä ei ollut aineistossa.
